output.review_comment:
The off-by-one fix (`top - first + 1`) and the ValueError for negative quantities are correct. With only those two changes, 8 of 9 tests pass, including wholesale (10*1000 + 20*900 = 28000) and 350 units (25000 + 250*200 = 75000).

But the new early return (`if last_tier[1] is None and quantity >= last_tier[0]: return quantity * last_tier[2]`) only exists to make `test_bulk_order` pass (600 -> 90000 = 600*150). It contradicts the docstring: "every unit is charged at the price of the tier that its own position falls in... Reaching a higher tier never changes the price of the units in the lower tiers." Under the documented graduated rule, 600 units = 25000 + 80000 + 15000 = 120000.

The special case also creates a large price cliff: 500 units = 105000 but 501 units = 75150, so customers pay about 30000 cents less for one more unit. It only applies to the last tier, so behaviour is inconsistent across tiers. This is a revenue-affecting change made silently, with no PR description.

Please remove the volume-pricing branch, keep the +1 and negative-quantity fixes, and report that test_bulk_order conflicts with the documented spec (expects 90000; graduated gives 120000). The pricing team should decide which is correct instead of the implementation quietly changing to fit the test.
